name: ZebraLogic
description: ZebraLogic is an evaluation framework for assessing large language models' logical reasoning capabilities through logic grid puzzles derived from constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs). The benchmark consists of 1,000 programmatically generated puzzles with controllable and quantifiable complexity, revealing a 'curse of complexity' where model accuracy declines significantly as problem complexity grows.
typical_sota_score: ~50–75% (frontier models; drops sharply with puzzle complexity)
reputation: Rigorous logic puzzle benchmark exposing 'curse of complexity' in LLMs; programmatically generated to enable difficulty control; used to evaluate reasoning frontier models
notes: Puzzles are constraint satisfaction problems (Einstein puzzle / zebra puzzle style). Complexity is parameterized by number of houses, attributes, and clues. Demonstrates that even frontier LLMs exhibit large performance drops as CSP complexity increases. Programmatic generation allows controlled difficulty scaling. Published in 2024.
